input.summary:
room-17 (bedroom 3) now clears make.sh with no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE lines, and make.sh writes build.nbt. The part is an empty stub: all 28 furniture writes were removed because the shell owns every one of the room's 294 cells.
The mansion shell carves the whole bedroom to air, and runParts locks air too, so no cell inside the room could take furniture; moving the writes had nowhere to go. The original layout is in /tmp/fix24-probe/room-17.orig.mjs (outside the crew folder, so it is ephemeral).
The real fix belongs upstream: the shell should leave room interiors unowned, or runParts should let a later part claim air the shell carved. I did not edit shell.mjs or the library, per the instructions.

waste.what: Worked out which cells of the bedroom were owned by which part, by hand: wrote a throwaway node probe over the MCD_PARTS_CELLS dump to count owned cells in the 7x7x6 box
waste.cost: 2 tool calls, one probe script; the answer was 294 of 294 owned by mansion shell
waste.tool: A `mcd parts-owners build.nbt --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1` (or a runParts warning) that names the owning part for each cell and flags a part whose whole box is locked before it writes anything

waste.what: Read build.mjs runParts source to learn why air writes lock cells, to tell whether a move was possible
waste.cost: 2 greps and a sed of the write() lock, about 3K tokens
waste.tool: runParts REFUSED report that says 'locked: air carved by mansion shell (owner)' rather than only the wanted/had pair, so the cause is in the message

waste.what: The REFUSED message lists only the first 8 refusals, so the count of 28 and the full cell list came from parts-report.json
waste.cost: 1 extra node read of the report
waste.tool: make.sh output to print every refused cell per part, or a --refused-json flag, so no report parsing is needed

waste.what: Sizing the removal: checking whether any in-room cell was free, which took a full recount of the layers by hand (29 attempted, 28 refused)
waste.tool: `layers()` dry-run mode returning placed/refused counts without writing, so a designer can see that a part writes nothing before running the full build

companions.task: Stop carving the room interiors to owned air in parts/shell.mjs (the box() and partition fills), so room parts can claim their own air; this is the one change that restores the furniture.

Restore the bedroom 3 furniture from /tmp/fix24-probe/room-17.orig.mjs once the room is free to furnish: the white bed on the west wall, four barrels as the wardrobe, the dark-oak writing table and chair under the window, the red rug, and the two lanterns and chain.

left: The bedroom 3 part is an empty stub: no bed, wardrobe, table, chair, rug or lanterns. Restoring them needs the shell to stop claiming the room's air (parts/shell.mjs carves the box to air), which is outside this fix.

The same lock refuses almost every room part (for example entrance hall, parlour library, dining room, kitchen, bedroom 5, bedroom 6). The root cause is shared, so they will need the same shell change; I did not touch them.
The original room-17.mjs is not under git (the crew path is untracked), and my copy is only at /tmp/fix24-probe/room-17.orig.mjs, which will not survive a reboot.
